{{Short description|Psychology concept}}
{{context|date=April 2016}}

The '''ideographic approach''' refers to the idea in [[psychology]] proposed by [[Brysbaert|Marc Brysbaert]] that the conclusions of a study stay limited to the phenomenon under study.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Brysbaert|title=Historical and Conceptual Issues in Psychology|pages=379|year=2009}}</ref> It also focuses on the importance of individual traits when determining [[behavior]] instead of group norms.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Freeman|first1=Arthur|title=Clinical Psychology: Integrating Science and Practice|url=https://archive.org/details/clinicalpsycholo00free|url-access=limited|last2=Felgoise|first2=Stephanie H.|last3=Davis|first3=Denise D.|date=2008|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|isbn=978-0-470-19055-5|location=Hoboken, NJ|pages=[https://archive.org/details/clinicalpsycholo00free/page/n175 155]}}</ref> It reinforces the position that the study of the individual is the most effective method of understanding behavior.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Association|first=Research and Education|title=The Best Test Preparation for the Advanced Placement Examination in Psychology|date=1995|publisher=Research & Education Assoc.|isbn=978-0-87891-883-6|location=|pages=213}}</ref>

== Background ==
A major tradition in behavioral psychology is concerned with the variables and how one's characteristics are abstracted from other people's.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last1=Deaux|first1=Kay|title=The Oxford Handbook of Personality and Social Psychology|last2=Snyder|first2=Mark|date=2018|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-022483-7|location=New York|pages=702}}</ref> The ideographic approach emerged from the position among pioneers in personality psychology that focuses on the study of individuality.<ref name=":0" />

== Methodologies ==
The ideographic approach often use qualitative methodologies in its study of small number of individuals rather than make generalizations out of information collected from a large quantitative database.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Archer|first1=John|title=Sex and Gender|url=https://archive.org/details/sexgenderndediti00arch|url-access=limited|last2=Lloyd|first2=Barbara|date=2002|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0-521-63533-2|location=Cambridge|pages=[https://archive.org/details/sexgenderndediti00arch/page/n29 14]}}</ref> The methods operate according to the idea that each person is like no other person.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Lerner|first=Richard|title=Handbook of Child Psychology and Developmental Science, Theory and Method, Seventh Edition|date=2015|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|isbn=978-1-118-95297-9|location=Hoboken, NJ|pages=638}}</ref>

The psychological literature distinguishes ideographic approach from the [[nomothetic]] laws, which are concerned with the general perspective.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Roeckelein|first=Jon E.|title=Dictionary of Theories, Laws, and Concepts in Psychology|url=https://archive.org/details/dictionarytheori00roec|url-access=limited|date=1998|publisher=Greenwood Publishing Group|isbn=978-0-313-30460-6|location=Westport, CT|pages=[https://archive.org/details/dictionarytheori00roec/page/n278 249]|language=en}}</ref>
